candidates.title: [Bug]: runtime crash (nil pointer dereference) after `trap checkpanic` inside a nested block
[Bug]: compiler crash (nil pointer in semtypes.newFieldPairs) when an included method is overridden with a return type of the class itself
[Bug]: compiler crash (nil CompilerContext in xmlParser) on an XML template attribute without a quoted value
candidates.body:
### Description
An XML template whose attribute value is not quoted (an interpolation `k=${...}`, or no value at all, `<a k/>`) crashes the compiler. The XML parser tries to report an internal error with a nil `*CompilerContext`. Related malformed inputs such as `<a k=v/>` and `<a k=${"v"}>` correctly report "missing double quote token".

### Steps to Reproduce
Save the following as `repro.bal` and run `go run ./cli/cmd run repro.bal`:

```ballerina
public function main() {
    xml v = xml `<a k=${"v"}/>`; // @error
    _ = v;
}
```

**Actual:**
```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x8 pc=0x8c6716]

goroutine 1 [running]:
context.(*CompilerContext).addDiagnostic(0x0, ...) context/context.go:268
context.(*CompilerContext).InternalError(...) context/context.go:255
parser.(*abstractParser).internalError(...) parser/parser.go:127
parser.(*xmlParser).parseXMLCharacterSet parser/xml_parser.go:448
parser.(*xmlParser).parseAttributeValue parser/xml_parser.go:271
parser.(*xmlParser).parseXMLAttribute parser/xml_parser.go:253
```

**Expected:** A compile-time syntax error on the marked line, not a crash. The same applies to `xml v = xml `<a k/>`;`.

**Spec reasoning:** §6.6.2: the template is parsed using the `content` production of the W3C XML Recommendation. There an interpolation can only stand for characters in CharData or AttValue, and AttValue must be quoted (`Attribute ::= Name Eq AttValue`), so both inputs are ill-formed and must be rejected with a diagnostic. A compiler panic is never acceptable.

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ da51086fe71a11ce6d8243cc03ca54b3f598327e

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux (x86_64), Go 1.27.1; interpreter run as `go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`.

### Related area
Parser

### Related issue(s) (optional)
None found. #1167 (closed) is a different parser nil-pointer crash (st.findToken/parseCompUnit path).

Examples: #1468, #1047, #1149, #1634, #1215, #1511, #1091, #1347, #1669, #1565, #1487, #1457, #1262, #1046, #1054, #895, #1217, #1148, #1471, #1134, #1026, #1214, #1512, #1131, #1374, #1395, #1043. Candidates found but NOT carried through the duplicate-check/validation pipeline because the limit was reached (worth checking next run): (a) a lock held across a yield (runtime:sleep or wait inside the lock body) deadlocks another non-isolated strand or named worker contending for the same lock; the program hangs forever and ignores SIGTERM (reproducer: two `start bump()` with `lock { int t = counter; runtime:sleep(0.01); counter = t + 1; }`; making bump isolated works). (b) `getAttributes()` on a `readonly & xml:Element` returns a map whose read-only bit is off (§5.3.2); the duplicate check says it is new, but it was not spec-validated. (c) An XML template accepts the reserved PI target `<?xml a?>` and `]]>` in text, while xml:fromString rejects both; the duplicate check says it is new, related to #1587 and #1588. (d) Variant of #1168: a panic in a callee called inside a lock body, trapped by the caller, leaves the lock held. subset10.md contradicts itself about whether `readonly` classes are supported (Class definition bullet vs Object/class definitions restriction).
